items.title: New Official $130 Elden Ring Release Confirmed for Fall 2026
items.summary: Elden Ring fans officially have a new release to look forward to in Fall 2026, with a big $130 price tag.
items.content:
New Official $130 Elden Ring Release Confirmed for Fall 2026 From GameRant (Written by Daniel Morris) on September 5, 2026 | OpenCritic

FromSoftware's Elden Ring has cultivated an enormous fanbase that's always on the lookout for new releases. There's some great news for fans, after a surprise new Elden Ring release was officially confirmed for Fall 2026, giving the community something to look forward to this year.

2022's Game of the Year Award-winning Elden Ring marked the next major innovation in FromSoftware's Soulslike formula, making it open-world for the first time. The game was an enormous critical and commercial success, setting up Elden Ring to be the next major FromSoftware IP. Interest in the franchise has not waned, either. Elden Ring 's recent Switch 2 release was a big hit , proving it still has the potential to reach new audiences despite its existing success.

Elden Ring remains a cultural hit, and its Switch 2 release makes starting your journey into the Lands Between easier than ever.

A new trio of 1/3 scale replica helmets based on three featured in the Elden Ring franchise is now available for pre-order on Sideshow from manufacturer PureArts. The first is based on Malenia, Blade of Miquella, typically seen as one of Elden Ring's toughest bosses. This stands at 6.7 inches, as does the second,...

items.title: Video: Digital Foundry Delivers Its Tech Review For Elden Ring On Switch 2
items.content:
After being delayed to " allow time for performance adjustments ", Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition finally arrived on the Switch 2 last month. So, was it worth the wait?

Digital Foundry has now taken a look and confirms the delay has been "immensely beneficial to the quality of the final release".

Digital Foundry: "It's a successful port that may not trouble the user with the higher-end visual experience enjoyed by other current-gen hardware, but you are broadly getting the PS4 feature set with improved frame-rates, higher resolutions on average, and much faster loading times - and, of course, you're getting a decent handheld experience too."

The Switch 2 version has no graphics mode toggle, meaning all visuals are "essentially set in stone from boot up".

In terms of resolution, in docked, you're looking at a dynamic 720p - 1080p range, while portable play runs between 432p - 864p. As for the frame rate, the Switch 2 version runs at a 40fps cap, but it's not "sustainable for any length of play" and "typical play rests much more often at 30-35fps in docked", with "portable performance in a similar ballpark".

Loading times are also a "highlight" on Switch 2, which proves to be significantly faster than its "last-gen rivals". You can find out more about the Switch 2 version in Digital Foundry's video and in our own review here on Nintendo Life:

Digital Foundry A solid release - but lacking current-gen visual features.

items.title: FromSoftware's first-ever player romance builds on "the maidens in Elden Ring," says Hidetaka Miyazaki: "It's a transient, ephemeral love, which is maybe a motif I'm striving for"
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter I already think the standard FromSoftware boss fight in which you're more likely to die the closer you get to touching someone is romantic in the way it makes my palms sweat. So I'm eager to learn if director Hidetaka Miyazaki will be able to scrunch my heart until it explodes with The Duskbloods , which will feature the first overt romance between players in a FromSoftware game.

Switch 2 multiplayer game The Duskbloods is set against the unnatural Dusk of Humanity, where up to eight players filled with powerful blood slash each other in the pursuit of a deeper red. But you don't only have to murder your opponents – you can marry them, too, with the Love Ephemeral sigil that allows one player to actually get down on one knee, take another's hands, and emote their devotion. It might be the most obviously romantic gesture in FromSoftware history, though Miyazaki doesn't necessarily see it that way.

He tells The Guardian in a new interview, "I feel it's less a traditional romance and more a sense of secure trust with a character in the world, and that's something I personally yearn for." And he's right, this is an option given to you repeatedly throughout the FromSoftware catalogue: put your delicate faith in a chosen one, even when you're among bewitched lands where delicate things are picked and burned.

2016's Dark Souls 3 allows players to marry Anri of Astora with the Ring of the Evil Eye, and 2022's Elden Ring makes a marriage alliance possible with Ranni the Witch – provided you slide the Dark Moon Ring onto her chilled porcelain finger. The different firekeepers, shrine maidens, and one special doll throughout Dark Souls and Bloodborne are also technically locked in these practical relationships with you as they remain committed to letting you level up. All these NPCs also have at least some degree of influence over their game's story events or endings, so pursuing them is prudent game-playing, too.

But since The Duskbloods' marriage occurs between two players rather than a player and NPC, it's more of a wild rose… or wildfire. Some The Duskbloods network test players report being killed by opponents while performing Love Ephemeral before they can squeak out a proposal speech, with one Reddit comment saying, "People are too aggressive when theres no reason to be! Im also looking for love."

Parts of The Duskbloods are "similar to a lot of RPG elements you might find in a tabletop RPG" Hidetaka Miyazaki says The Duskbloods is full of ideas FromSoftware couldn't fit into Dark Souls Even after Elden Ring exploded, Hidetaka Miyazaki says FromSoftware doesn't make games for anyone Love and pain are counterweights, of course. But it seems like Miyazaki would rather not have The Duskbloods' marriage alliances be so contentious. He thinks of it the way a king surveys a soldier with her weapon.

"It's not necessarily a romantic pairing," the developer says, "it's having someone that you can ultimately rely on. This concept is carried through from characters like the maidens in Elden Ring… it's a transient, ephemeral love, which is maybe a motif I'm striving for."

But even if you tell yourself you're only in it for the convenience, handing your heart to another always comes with the risk of severe disappointment. I imagine this is doubly true if you both have guns.

Nintendo denies The Duskbloods' September release date in the least convincing way possible .

Ashley Bardhan Social Links Navigation Senior Writer Ashley is a Senior Writer at GamesRadar+. She's been a staff writer at Kotaku and Inverse, too, and she's written freelance pieces about horror and women in games for sites like Rolling Stone, Vulture, IGN, and Polygon. When she's not covering gaming news, she's usually working on expanding her doll collection while watching Saw movies one through 11.

items.title: Review: Switch 2 Elden Ring: PS4 Visuals, Improved Frame-Rate and Faster Loading Times
items.summary: A solid release - but lacking current-gen visual features.
items.content:
A solid release - but lacking current-gen visual features.

After initial controversy around sub-standard performance in pre-release code, the Tarnished Edition of Elden Ring is finally available for Switch 2 - and the substantial delay has paid off. After its delay from an original late 2025 release, From Software has delivered a robust package that includes the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, additional starting classes and exclusive cosmetic items for the player and their mount - contained within a 40GB install size. But what kind of Elden Ring experience are Switch 2 users getting and is it more PS4 than PS5?

Excepting the handheld and docked configurations, there are no graphics modes to wade through here, making our life a little easier. While in TV mode, Elden Ring runs at a dynamic 720p - 1080p range, matching the upper bounds of the the original PlayStation 4 version. Surprisingly the max 1080p figure is well-held across most of Limgrave, though 720p appears in rainy woodland regions - like the Weeping Peninsula. Another key distinction is that Switch 2 doesn't lean on dynamic scaling as heavily as PS4, meaning most matched shots are clearer by comparison. Also curiously, there's no DLSS used here, with From instead opting for its own anti-aliasing solution. The end result is image quality that looks extremely similar to the PlayStation 4 version of the game when both run at 1080p - but it's tantalising to imagine how Nvidia's upscaler could have benefitted the port.

In terms of "settings", Switch 2 is a almost a mirror image of the PlayStation 4 code, with identical textures, world layout, shadow quality, along with the same screen-space reflection implementation. The only discrepancy you might spot is in grass density, which favours PS4 while looking to the mid-to-far range. It’s ever-so-slightly higher than Switch 2’s in density by comparison, but it takes a close zoom to pick out. Meanwhile Switch 2 enjoys an advantage in asset streaming while travelling through the world on horseback - where trees and bushes struggle to load consistently on PS4's HDD at such pace. Stand still however, and the scenery resolves with identical results. The two are almost 1:1 - while comparisons against PS5 show what's left on the table in higher-end settings. You get more lush, foliage-rich environments from the current-gen versions - including Series S - which are not present on Switch 2.

It looks like Elden Ring, it feels like Elden Ring, but the Switch 2 port does share some of the CPU-based restrictions seen on last-gen and Series S. When numerous enemies are on-screen, animation decimation is in play, causing movement on those characters to appear akin to a stop-motion sequence. It's not a constant, it only happens intermittently, but it is there, just as it is on other lower power consoles.

Handheld play gives Switch 2 fewer GPU resources, requiring further cutbacks. First up, the dynamic 720p - 1080p range while docked drops to a lower 432p - 864p range while portable. Again, typically it's at the max 864p figure around Limgrave and still looks sharp enough on the smaller screen - but the Weeping Peninsula will trigger a res drop. Otherwise, foliage density is pruned back a setting below docked mode, while SSR is also tweaked - though at least it's still there. Shadow quality also takes a hit.

The frame-rate strategy for the Switch 2 is a touch bizarre. The bottom line is that Switch 2 runs with a 40 frames per second cap. As a design choice, this 40fps cap makes perfect sense for a 120Hz handheld panel or a living room display running at the same refresh rate, but only if it can sustain the frame-rate target with even frame-pacing - historically, not From Software's strongest suit. Gunning for 40fps is entirely unique to this platform, given that PS4 and Xbox One ran with a 30fps cap, and the current-gen systems run entirely unlocked to 60.

The reality is that 40fps play is only truly possible while looking at the sky, or during parts of less taxing dungeons. It's simply not sustainable for any length of play in the open world - and when it does, those frame-times are inconsistent too. Ultimately, typical play rests much more often at 30-35fps while running docked. We've even spotted some lurches into the high 20s around the Caelid area - occasional as they are - which may hint towards troubled performance levels later on. Portable performance is in a similar ballpark going by eye, and based on the first five hours of play, we're getting similar dips to 25fps causing judder there too. It's not ideal by any means. But, in the wider context of Elden Ring's frame-rate on other platforms - like PS4 and especially Xbox One - Switch 2 is a more performant release by comparison.

Loading times are a highlight for the Switch 2, which proves significantly faster than its last-gen rivals. Moving from the Roundtable Hold to the First Steps site of grace takes roughly 12.4 seconds on Switch 2. This is considerably faster than the Xbox Series S at 18.6 seconds and significantly quicker than the PS4, which, constrained by its mechanical hard drive, takes 35.6 seconds. While it does not beat the 7.1-second load time of the PlayStation 5, the performance is impressive and helps maintain immersion while exploring the Lands Between.

Summing up our experience with the game, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is thankfully nowhere near as "tarnished" as initial media suggested - the delay has proven immensely beneficial to the quality of the final release and there's no issue in recommending it. It's a successful port that may not trouble the user with the higher-end visual experience enjoyed by other current-gen hardware, but you are broadly getting the PS4 feature set with improved frame-rates, higher resolutions on average, and much faster loading times - and, of course, you're getting a decent handheld experience too. An optional 30fps cap would have been welcome but From Software's history in delivering that with a consistent level of frame-pacing is essentially non-existent so while the existing 40fps capped solution is not perfect, it is likely preferable.

Three years on, Elden Ring's performance problems remain unaddressed

items.title: Hidetaka Miyazaki Finally Addresses The Feet Jokes
items.summary: Miyazaki doesn't really understand where the rumor came from.
items.content:
By James Lucas Published Sep 4, 2026, 6:31 AM EDT James Lucas is an Executive Editor at TheGamer who has worked in professional journalism since 2018. A Newcastle University graduate with a degree in Journalism, Media, and Culture, they have written hundreds of guides, news stories, and original reports, with bylines in IGN, NME, GaymingMag, and VG247, sourcing interviews with studio heads, legendary industry figures, prominent actors, and more. An expert on FPS games, Soulslikes, RPGs, and survival horror, James has intimate knowledge of a wide variety of titles, providing in-depth coverage and exclusive profiles. Some of the games they have extensively covered include: Half-Life 3, Counter-Strike, Elden Ring, and Fallout. They pride themselves on their consistently thorough research, leveraging nearly a decade of industry experience. You can reach them at James.t@thegamer.com Sign in to your TheGamer account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Hidetaka Miyazaki is known for his liminal, dystopian worlds. Ruined civilizations erected on the skeletons of bygone people, dotted with miserable miscreants who chuckle through gritted teeth at forlorn warriors facing insurmountable odds. Cycles repeat and old wounds reopen. There’s a thread through Demon’s Souls to Bloodborne to Elden Ring — a signature style. And then there’s feet. A lot of feet.

It’s become a running joke over the years that Miyazaki has a thing for toes . NPCs, bosses, nobody is exempt. The Maiden in Black walks around barefoot, Crossbreed Priscilla waits in the Painted World with her ravenous dogs out, and Malenia even has sculpted golden toes. It’s an enigma. But, finally, in an interview with TheGamer’s former editor-in-chief Kirk McKeand for The Guardian , Miyazaki addressed the rumors. And I can’t tell if the confusion is Miyazaki embodying the unreliable narrator of his games, or genuine bewilderment that the internet thinks he’s fascinated by women’s feet.

Unprompted, when asked about the recurring motif of hands throughout his games, Miyazaki said, “It’s not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of — maybe it’s something subconscious coming through. Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet , but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from. I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe.”

McKeand notes that Miyazaki-directed games have featured at least six barefoot women, practically making him the Tarantino of the industry. But it doesn’t appear to be a deliberate fascination — an internal quota he sneakily gets FromSoftware designers to hit. ‘Yeah… but have we considered that this woman shouldn’t have boots on?’ There may even be something human about that physical connection and intimacy. Or maybe he just likes feet.

This is hardly the article to wax lyrical about the optimism found in despair that FromSoftware’s worlds leave us grasping for. The real takeaway is that Miyazaki has seen the memes. He knows we’re all joking about his loving feet every single time a cutscene pans just a little too far down and we see toes.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review – A Masterpiece in Your Hands
items.summary: The Elden Ring Tarnish Edition brings together the beloved ARPG and its excellent DLC as one package for the Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
Back when it was released in 2024, I gave Elden Ring a score of 98. Four years later, and considering I have well over 1000 hours of play time on PC and PS5, I still wonder if my score was too low. For me, Elden Ring is the absolute pinnacle of FromSoftware’s design philosophy and the gold standard for open world action games. It’s now hard to put myself in the shoes of someone playing Elden Ring for the first time. Considering that around 30-40% of Switch 2 owners don’t have a gaming PC or other high-end console, there’s a good chance that gamers picking up the Tarnished Edition will be dropping in for the first time. Lucky them.

The Tarnished Edition brings together the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, itself maybe the best DLC ever released for a game. It also includes a handful of new weapons, two new classes, and skins for Torrent, the player’s mount. These add-ons are also available for $4.99 for PC and console games who already own the game. Accessing the game’s co-op and PvP features means having a subscription to Nintendo Switch Online.

If you’ve already played Elden Ring on PC or another console, you’re probably just wondering how it fares on Nintendo Switch 2. Elden Ring on the go sounds like a dream come true. The good news is that it runs just fine, if you’re willing to accept some limitations. Frame rates are capped at 30fps. Textures and ray tracing are a little simplified and a bit blurry, especially in handheld mode. On the other hand, the beauty of Elden Ring is in its art, character and environmental designs. It doesn’t depend on photorealism. In combat, the 30fps throttle is a little more frustrating, and framerates dip a little in the more intense boss battles. Bottom line, the Switch 2 is powerful enough to run Elden Ring and players will have the full experience.

If you’ve never played a FromSoftware game, be prepared for some narrative confusion. The developer is known for stories that are opaque, dense with lore and full of sadness, darkness, and fading hope. With an assist by George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring’s narrative tells of a shattered world. The demigod children of Queen Marika have torn the realm apart. The player takes on the role of a Tarnished, tasked with slaying the corrupt demigods and claiming the title of Elden Lord.

It should be noted that with any FromSoft game, there are fans who dive deep into the lore. At the other end, there are even more players who simply ignore most of the narrative and focus on exploration and combat. Elden Ring rewards either approach. For anyone who’s confused, there’s an immense amount of material online about the characters and their complex relationships.

When it comes to action and combat, Elden Ring represents a major step forward and brings together mechanics explored in other games from the developer. There are few — if any — action RPGs with boss battles as finely tuned as those in Elden Ring. The number of weapons, armor sets, and ways to use magic is staggering in its variety. Like most RPGs, Elden Ring has starting classes but these are largely ignored by players past the first few hours. That said, the Tarnished Edition adds two extremely viable classes in the form of the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight.

Souls games have a well-earned reputation for difficulty, and FromSoftware has resisted adding difficulty options. That’s because they’re built in. Especially in Elden Ring, if players are struggling there are always areas to visit and lower level enemies to kill. There are other weapons or spells to try. The game’s system for summoning Spirit Ashes allows players to call on extremely competent AI companions to help out. Compared to exacting platformers where there is no margin for error, FromSoft’s games feel, if not forgiving, at least balanced and fair.

Outside of combat, exploration is extremely rewarding thanks to a fast travel system and Torrent, your mount. While Elden Ring’s map isn’t the biggest open world it feels immense due to layers of verticality and subterranean areas to explore. No area feels too empty and between the labyrinthine Legacy Dungeons and open landscapes, there’s always something to discover or fight. The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC added a significant amount of new content to an already massive game.

If you haven’t played Elden Ring, and the Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 has enticed you, please make the leap. I envy you seeing it all for the first time. If you have the game on other consoles or PC and don’t own something like a Steam deck or ROG Ally, the Elden Ring you love is there and intact, but with the visual downgrade that you probably expect. In the end, more Elden Ring is a very good thing.

***Switch 2 code provided by the publisher for review***

items.title: An Obscure Setting Keeps Ruining Elden Ring: Nightreign For Me
items.summary: I do not want to know about any of this
items.content:
I have over 150 hours in Elden Ring Nightreign , and as I have admitted before on this website, I am not very good at it. Over the course of that 150 hours, I think I’ve spent a lot of time being carried by both my partner and our trios pal, who plays Guardian consistently and is great at making sure my wimpy Recluse/Scholar-ass doesn’t die (or, when dead, gets revived promptly). Together, we have taken 150 hours to very slowly kill almost every regular Night Boss in the game, leaving just the DLC’s Dreglord unslain at this time. It is likely due in no small part to my lack of skill that it has taken this long, though I also somewhat blame our busy lives and the fact that we often take long breaks and forget how to play.

But earlier this week, I have found another culprit to pin this on, and her name is Nat. NAT Type.

What the hell is NAT type? I’m still not 100-percent sure despite it being explained to me repeatedly. From what I can gather, it’s some mysterious, internet-related setting that determines how online games connect to the internet and to other people playing those games on the internet. I had literally never heard of it prior to Monday of this week, and I wish I still didn’t know about it.

The reason NAT type came up is because both my partner and I have been having constant issues with disconnects in Elden Ring Nightreign for several months now, for seemingly no particular reason. Almost every single match, one or both of us would disconnect. First, there would be up to 20 seconds or so where our characters would be stuck running around the world, unable to do damage or affect anything in them. Then, we’d actually get kicked out, and have to go through the grueling process of getting back to the menu screen, clicking through some menus, and then reloading back into the game. And because it’s Nightreign , this would be a huge disadvantage. We’d end up wasting something like a full minute of time, and when we got back in we’d either respawn somewhere vaguely near where we disconnected, with all our runes (including one whole lost level) dumped somewhere else for us to go waste time picking up. Or, if we were at the end of a night, we’d just respawn dead, and whoever was still connected would have to maneuver over to us while still fighting the boss and try to get us back up.

This has been infuriating! I tolerated it for a long time, because I enjoy Nightreign , but it really, really feels bad to be the one dragging the group down in this manner.

We tried everything to fix it. Whatever solution you’re about to suggest, we did it. We checked our connections. We reset the router so many times. We changed who hosted the match. We screwed around with all sorts of settings. We made sure we were on wired connections. Etc etc etc. None of it worked.

Finally, my partner did some dedicated research and discovered that something called our NAT type was the problem. Apparently, our NAT types were set to Moderate, which can cause issues with online multiplayer. From what I can figure out, you can change your NAT type properly by following a bunch of complex steps dealing with your router. Or for us on Xbox, we were able to spam the “Test NAT” function in the settings until eventually it swapped our NAT type to Open. When we played hours later, my partner’s was fixed, but mine was not. We checked the settings again, and mine had reverted back to Moderate. We spammed Test NAT again, got it to Open, and we’ve had uninterrupted matches ever since.

So I guess now before I play Nightreign , I have to check this setting every time? This is ridiculous! Why does stuff work like this? I feel like I shouldn’t have to do deep research into an obscure-for-most-people internet setting just to play an online game as it’s intended to be played. I’m not trying to do anything wacky here, I’m literally just getting into a co-op game with two other people, all of whom have excellent internet connections. Most people should not have to know about NAT type, or UPNP (whatever that is) or IPV6 or any of the other weird acronyms I saw while researching this. Like yes, I could probably work this out with time if I sat down and messed around with it long enough, but I don’t have time to do technological research just to bonk a stupid death goop monster around a giant arena without making my friend solo him for 60 seconds at a time at random.

If you’re having trouble with disconnections in Nightreign or Elden Ring PvP stuff or anything like that, consider melting your brain and learning about NAT type. I don’t recommend it, but it did result in me being able to play Nightreign without (unnecessary) frustration, improving my evenings dramatically. However, as soon as I beat up Dreglord, I intend to forget everything I know (very little) about NAT type again for the rest of my life.

items.title: Elden Ring Director Doesn't 'Have A Thing For Feet'
items.content:
There’s a rather lovely interview at The Guardian today with Hidetaka Miyazaki, director of Elden Ring and The Duskbloods and president of FromSoftware. In it, he talks about the themes of his work: ruin and rebirth, yearning, hope and hopelessness, and so forth.

He also talks about hands. And, seemingly unprompted, feet.

In the interview, Miyazaki is asked specifically about the imagery of hands in The Duskbloods and Elden Ring , such as the giant hand-shaped enemies in the latter and the close-up of one hand reaching for another in the introductory cinematic for the former. Miyazaki says he’s not really consistently aware that he employs such imagery in his work, but he then takes an interesting angle as he ponders this thought further:

“Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from. I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe.”

Okay! You know! I had never really thought about this before, but sure, let’s go. This is how I learned that my editor wrote about this topic four whole years ago , and it’s been a meme since well before then. It’s true that there are just a lot of barefooted characters in Miyazaki’s games , and we often get cutscenes or close-ups of those bare feet, or at least get to see them very well-rendered and artfully done. So I guess fans have theorized repeatedly over the years that this is a thing for Miyazaki.

I think I mostly buy Miyazaki’s answer, though I’m amused that he seems to be overly preoccupied with what people are saying about him online. I do like the notion that the giant, horrifying enemy hands in Elden Ring are him “trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe.” If I think about it for a bit I can probably understand what he means, but it’s rather difficult to concentrate on the symbolism when one of these fuckers has burst out of the ground and grabbed me.

items.title: Quick Review: ELDEN RING TARNISHED EDITION (Switch 2)
items.summary: Story and Gameplay We got our review copy a bit late but wanted to share our quick thoughts on the the highly anticipated Switch 2 edition of ELDEN RING. This is an absolute modern classic, and there
items.content:
We got our review copy a bit late but wanted to share our quick thoughts on the the highly anticipated Switch 2 edition of ELDEN RING. This is an absolute modern classic, and there's not much to say that we didn't cover in our original review beyond reminding everyone, Soulslike fan or not, that this game deserves to be played on any platform. The Switch 2 version isn't perfect, but it's extremely well done. The Tarnished Edition content is welcome, though not a game-changer by any means. New starting classes, new armor, etc. are a nice touch, but it's the base game that remains one of the best ever made.

The audiovisual presentation is stunning whether you're playing in handheld mode or docked. I just wish more Switch 2 ports had a performance mode option to reduce graphical fidelity and try to hit 50 or 60 fps. Either way, this Switch 2 port is definitely polished and I’m glad we got a solid and smooth version of this gem.

The soundtrack and sound effects remain some of the best in the industry. No complaints here and fans will be pleased at this sonic landscape.

At $79.99 MSRP, the price is a bit of a mystery, since the original game was $59.99. Yes, the DLC and new content are included, but it still feels like a big asking price and knocks our score down a bit. Beyond that and the performance mode option I wish were here, there's little to complain about.

The Switch 2 version of ELDEN RING is finally upon us, and whether you've played it to death before or never touched it, this version rocks and I highly recommend it. Playing through it again reminded me how much I love this masterpiece and FromSoftware in general. Every Switch 2 owner deserves to have this in their library, even if they have to wait for an eventual (maybe) sale.

items.title: Elden Ring on the Switch 2 isn’t tarnished
items.summary: An excellent new way to play.
items.content:

The latest version of the open-world epic has me hooked all over again.

Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Senior entertainment editor Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Share Gift Image: Bandai Namco Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

FromSoftware is hoping to make a splash on the Switch 2 later this year when it launches The Duskbloods , a gothic competitive multiplayer game that’s unlike anything the studio has made before . But before that, Switch 2 owners have a chance to experience the studio’s biggest hit for the first time thanks to a port of Elden Ring and its expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree . For the most part, the new version — called the “Tarnished Edition” — is the same game that captivated players in 2022 . But the shift in platform also makes it a particularly compelling way to explore the Lands Between.

Elden Ring differentiated itself from past FromSoft games by introducing a large open world shrouded in mystery and brimming with danger. And as we’ve learned over the years, open-world games work especially well on Nintendo’s hybrid console, letting you play in small bursts while in portable mode before settling in for grander adventures on your television. Nintendo made this point crystal clear launching the original Switch alongside The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , and the extra horsepower of the Switch 2 has been put to use for ports of gigantic games like Cyberpunk 2077 .

In many ways Elden Ring is an ideal test case for the Switch 2. It may be a few years old, but it’s a big and demanding game, one where every element matters. Wonky frame rates could mean death in battle, while dark or fuzzy graphics could allow a cave-dwelling creature to get the jump on you. I spent dozens of hours exploring and dying in the PS5 version of the game when it first launched, and I’ve since spent around 10 hours dabbling with the Switch 2 port. And while the Switch 2 edition isn’t the most technically impressive version of the game, it is one that runs just well enough to possibly be my favorite way to play.

Replaying the opening hours of Elden Ring is an interesting experience. It’s easy to forget just how unforgiving the game can be early on. You play as a weak little wretch known as a Tarnished, thrust into an expansive fantasy realm full of things that want to kill you. One of the first things you see is a giant gladiator riding a horse, and if you try to attack it you’ll die from a single swipe of its sword. It’s a powerful learning experience, and much of my time with the Switch 2 version of the game has been spent cowering in bushes and slaying flocks of giant bats in order to slowly level up my fledgling astrologer. I’ve made some progress — I finally took down Margit, the Fell Omen, the game’s first major boss, and I made it to the Roundtable to get a comforting hug from Fia — but mostly I’ve just been puttering around, cautiously poking at the edges of the world, slowly growing in both strength and confidence.

The most important thing about my experience so far is that the limitations of the hardware never had a negative impact. There are some Switch 2 drawbacks, like less detailed characters and some textures that look muddy or washed out. But these are all superficial things, and I found myself largely forgetting about them the more that I explored. I haven’t come across any issues of stuttering or frame rate drops, either in portable or TV mode. Which is all to say that Elden Ring performs well enough on the Switch 2 that, aside from the occasional long load, I haven’t spent much time thinking about the game’s performance at all.

Instead, I’ve found myself once again lost in the Lands Between, spending many of my waking moments reliving adventures or dreaming up where I want to go next. As with other big games on the Switch or its successor, the nature of the platform makes it easier to fit an adventure of this scale into my life. Sometimes, I grab the tablet and just spend 20 minutes clearing out a camp full of soldiers or seeking out the next Site of Grace, making incremental progress that will make life easier when I tuck in to explore for hours in TV mode.

This isn’t a new revelation about the Switch by any stretch. But with Elden Ring ’s sprawling landscape and unforgiving combat, it’s an ideal example of the type for how well this kind of open world can work on the Switch 2. And with The Duskbloods lurking in the shadows , it’s a great way to scratch that FromSoft itch while waiting for the studio’s next game.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition launches on the Nintendo Switch 2 on August 28th.

items.title: The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter
items.content:
Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring , a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
